text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- United States condemns Cambodia's Second Prime Minister Hun Sen for using force to oust rival Prince Norodom Ranariddh and says U.S. officials will meet prince in Washington.
- About 450 Singaporeans and foreigners flown into Singapore from war-torn Cambodia on C-130 transport planes of Republic of Singapore Air Force.
- Three panels formed to suggest names of people who might become nominated members of parliament.
- Former Merrill Lynch private banker Kevin Wallace and father-in-law released on bail in Hong Kong but dates set for them to report to police there.
- Philippine central bank dumps U.S. dollars to defend peso after report the authorities would discuss proposed devaluation sparks another speculative attack on peso.
- Burmese kyat plunges against dollar-denominated foreign exchange certificates forcing prices of imported goods to rise sharply, currency dealers and analysts say.
- Philippine President Fidel Ramos flatly rules out a peso devaluation and blames "outsiders" and "media disinformation campaign" for continuing speculative attacks on country's currency.

- Nervousness over regional currencies spills over into Singapore equities, sending benchmark Straits Times Industrials index to low of 1,971.96 points before it steadies somewhat to close for net loss of 24.26 points at 1,982.97.
- Retail and leisure mogul Ong Beng Seng weighing bid for Barney's Inc, U.S. luxury retailer now in financial distress.
- Inventory of wound-up television maker Funai Electric (Singapore) to be auctioned off next week.
- Thai authorities may bend rules on new banking licences to help Singapore's DBS Bank bid for majority stake in troubled Thai finance firm, local analyst says.
- Annual report award competition launched, with organisers putting focus on SESDAQ-listed companies this year.
